title: Legacy privileged access path does not consistently enforce MFA
framework_reference: UK GDPR Article 32(1)-(2); Article 5(1)(f) security context
condition: Three of 42 privileged identities remained able to use a legacy remote-access path without the approved MFA enforcement.
criteria_expected_state: Authentication safeguards for privileged access should be proportionate to the high impact of administrative compromise and consistently applied across access paths.
cause: Legacy VPN migration created an exception path that was not brought under equivalent conditional-access enforcement; compensating controls were not formally defined for all affected identities.
risk_consequence: Compromise of a privileged credential could enable unauthorised access to systems processing customer personal information, increasing confidentiality, integrity and account-security risk.
likelihood_rationale: The path is limited but internet/remote credential attack remains plausible.
impact_rationale: Privileged compromise could affect multiple critical customer systems and large volumes of restricted information.
recommendation: Retire or isolate the legacy path; enforce phishing-resistant or otherwise risk-appropriate MFA for privileged interactive access; define tightly controlled emergency-account exceptions; and monitor/report any remaining bypasses until closure.
management_response: Agreed. IAM will migrate vendor support to the modern access path and place break-glass accounts under enhanced monitoring with documented activation controls.
residual_risk_comment: To be reassessed after migration and independent retest.

title: Central monitoring does not cover two critical personal-data systems
framework_reference: UK GDPR Article 32(1)-(2); Article 5(1)(f) security context
condition: Two of 12 critical sources - Meridian Customer CRM audit logs and Privacy Case Management administrative activity - were retained locally but not centrally ingested or covered by Sentinel alerting.
criteria_expected_state: Security-relevant activity affecting restricted personal information should be available for timely detection, investigation and correlation at a level proportionate to risk.
cause: SIEM onboarding prioritised core transaction and identity systems; privacy/CRM administrative logs were left in a backlog without risk-based completion dates.
risk_consequence: Misuse or compromise of privileged access in the two systems may be detected late or require fragmented investigation, increasing the chance and duration of unauthorised processing.
likelihood_rationale: Local logs exist, but lack of central monitoring increases exposure to delayed detection.
impact_rationale: The systems hold customer case data and privacy-case evidence but are not the core banking transaction store.
recommendation: Risk-rank and onboard both sources to central monitoring, implement priority privileged/admin activity detections, confirm retention and time synchronisation, and add quarterly reconciliation of critical systems to SIEM coverage.
management_response: Agreed. SOC engineering has created onboarding work items for CRM and privacy-case administration logs.
residual_risk_comment: Local log access is a temporary detective fallback, not closure.

title: Critical core-banking restore testing evidence is incomplete
condition: Backups were operating, but one of four sampled critical backup sets - the core-banking platform - had no completed annual restore-test evidence in the prior 12 months.
criteria_expected_state: Recovery capability for critical personal-data processing should be periodically tested so the organisation can demonstrate timely restoration, not only backup-job success.
cause: The planned restore exercise was rescheduled twice because of release-calendar conflicts; governance did not escalate repeated deferral against the criticality of the service.
risk_consequence: A latent restore defect could remain undetected until a real disruption, extending loss of availability or access to customer information.
likelihood_rationale: Backups report successful and other restores passed, reducing likelihood, but untested core-banking recovery remains uncertain.
impact_rationale: Core banking is a critical customer-data and service dependency.
recommendation: Complete an end-to-end core-banking restore exercise against approved recovery objectives, record data-integrity validation, and require formal risk acceptance/escalation when critical restore tests are deferred.
management_response: Agreed. Recovery Engineering has reserved a controlled exercise window and will obtain business-owner sign-off on recovered data validation.
residual_risk_comment: No closure until completed restore evidence is independently reviewed.

title: Ongoing security assurance for a material CRM processor is overdue
condition: Northbridge CRM Services Ltd had not received its planned annual security assurance refresh since January 2025, and a penetration-test remediation item in the prior review had no documented closure evidence.
criteria_expected_state: A controller should maintain risk-proportionate assurance that a processor provides sufficient guarantees and continues to operate appropriate security measures, with identified weaknesses tracked to closure.
cause: Third-party risk scheduling focused on DORA/critical-service providers and did not preserve privacy-processor review cadence for this UK CRM relationship.
risk_consequence: MTFS may lack current assurance over security controls protecting customer information processed by a material supplier, weakening accountability and increasing exposure to undetected supplier control deterioration.
likelihood_rationale: No breach or confirmed control failure was identified; the issue is stale assurance and unresolved evidence.
impact_rationale: The processor holds material customer/case data and supports onboarding/privacy services.
recommendation: Complete a refreshed risk-based security assessment of Northbridge, obtain closure evidence for the prior penetration-test action, record subprocessor/transfer changes, and integrate privacy-processor review dates into the enterprise third-party assurance schedule.
management_response: Agreed. Supplier Risk and Privacy will run a joint assurance refresh and move the relationship to a single risk-based review calendar.
residual_risk_comment: Contractual controls remain in force; operating assurance is incomplete.

title: Critical and high vulnerabilities exceed approved remediation windows
condition: Ten of 27 Critical/High vulnerabilities on selected personal-data systems exceeded approved remediation windows at 31 July 2026, including four Critical items.
criteria_expected_state: Known vulnerabilities affecting personal-data processing should be assessed and remediated within risk-based timelines, with time-bound exceptions where treatment is delayed.
cause: Application release dependencies and incomplete ownership escalation allowed vulnerability tickets to age beyond SLA without consistent compensating-control or exception records.
risk_consequence: Known exploitable weaknesses may remain available to attackers for longer than risk appetite, increasing the probability of compromise, data exposure or service disruption.
likelihood_rationale: Exposure is known and aged but no active exploitation was evidenced in the synthetic sample.
impact_rationale: Affected systems support customer digital and CRM processing.
recommendation: Prioritise the four Critical items, enforce owner escalation before SLA breach, require documented time-bound exceptions with compensating controls, and introduce weekly aged-vulnerability reporting for restricted-data assets.
management_response: Agreed. Vulnerability Management will establish an executive escalation queue for Critical items and require formal exceptions for overdue High items.
